From droplet to raindrop

Cloud droplets are far too small to fall. This is how they grow heavy enough to reach the ground, and what shape they are when they do.

← Clouds are made of droplets

01Overview

Rain is one kind of : water released from clouds as rain, freezing rain, sleet, snow or hail.1

The droplets in a cloud are far too small to fall as rain. To reach the ground, they have to grow.2

02Droplets merge

Droplets bump into each other and join together, which is called . Millions of cloud droplets are needed to make a single raindrop.2,3

A drop leaves the cloud once it falls faster than the , the rising air inside the cloud.2

03The ice route

When a cloud holds ice crystals, the crystals can grow quickly by taking water from the cloud. This is called the .2

The crystals may fall as snow, or melt on the way down and fall as rain.2

04The shape of a raindrop

Raindrops are not shaped like teardrops. Small drops, with a radius under 1 millimetre, are round like a ball.1,2

  • At about 2 to 3 millimetres across, a falling drop is flat underneath, like a hamburger bun.
  • At about 4 to 5 millimetres, the dip in its bottom grows into a shape like a parachute.
  • Bigger still, the drop breaks up into smaller drops.

2

Remember

Takeaways

  • Cloud droplets must grow before they can fall.
  • They grow by merging, and in icy clouds by the Bergeron process.
  • Small raindrops are round; bigger ones flatten, hollow out and split.

In under a minute

Recap

  1. Cloud droplets are too small to fall, so they have to grow.
  2. They merge, and millions of them make one raindrop.
  3. In icy clouds, crystals grow fast and fall as snow, or melt into rain.
  4. Small raindrops are round, and big ones flatten and break apart.
